name: Puerto del Escudo – Italian memorial
story: The Escudo pass (about 1,000 m) carries the main road from Burgos to Santander over the Cantabrian range. When the Nationalist offensive on Santander opened on 14 August 1937, Italian CTV divisions attacked here. By 17 August they had taken the pass and linked up with other columns near San Miguel de Aguayo, encircling Republican units. The Santander front collapsed within days, and Santander fell on 26 August. Basque units surrendered to the Italians under the separate Santoña pact (24 August), which Franco did not honour. A pyramid-shaped memorial to the Italian dead still stands at the summit; the remains once kept there have since been moved.
see: A stone pyramid memorial beside the N-623 at the top of the pass, with wide mountain views.
plan: Pull in at the summit on the N-623 (Burgos–Santander). The road is often closed by snow in winter.

boxes.text: This is a Fascist-era monument; its future is debated under Spain's democratic memory legislation.
